# Retrieval ablation — measured results

**Corpus:** Microsoft Annual Reports FY2020–FY2025 (6 documents)
**Eval set:** 25 answerable questions across 5 tiers, 49 verbatim gold spans
**Scoring:** span containment — a question counts as retrieved if any chunk in the top *k* contains any of its gold spans
**Generated by:** `scripts/eval_retrieval.py`

Retrieval only. No generation, no LLM judge — this isolates whether the right
evidence reaches the model at all. Answer quality, faithfulness and refusal
behaviour are measured separately in step 11.

> **No fiscal-year filtering.** The gold data records which year each span
> belongs to, but passing that to the retriever would leak the answer — the
> system does not know the year at question time.

---

## recall@k

Fraction of the 25 questions where at least one gold span appeared in the top *k*.

| chunking | retriever | @1 | @3 | @5 | @10 |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| fixed | vector | 20% | 32% | 40% | 60% |
| fixed | bm25 | 28% | 52% | 52% | 56% |
| fixed | hybrid | 32% | 52% | 56% | 72% |
| fixed | **hybrid + rerank** | 52% | 76% | 92% | **96%** |
| structure_aware | vector | 16% | 44% | 56% | 76% |
| structure_aware | bm25 | 20% | 40% | 56% | 76% |
| structure_aware | hybrid | 20% | 52% | 72% | 80% |
| structure_aware | **hybrid + rerank** | 52% | 72% | 88% | **92%** |
| semantic | vector | 24% | 44% | 56% | 72% |
| semantic | bm25 | 28% | 48% | 64% | 72% |
| semantic | hybrid | 28% | 52% | 64% | 84% |
| semantic | **hybrid + rerank** | 44% | 68% | 92% | **100%** |

## span recall@k

Fraction of all 49 gold spans found — a stricter metric, and the honest one for
the multi-document and temporal tiers, where answering properly needs evidence
from several documents rather than any one of them.

| chunking | retriever | @1 | @3 | @5 | @10 |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| fixed | hybrid | 18% | 33% | 41% | 57% |
| fixed | hybrid + rerank | 33% | 51% | 61% | 69% |
| structure_aware | hybrid | 10% | 35% | 51% | 63% |
| structure_aware | hybrid + rerank | 35% | 51% | 59% | 71% |
| semantic | hybrid | 16% | 39% | 47% | 57% |
| semantic | hybrid + rerank | 33% | 45% | 65% | **76%** |

Every configuration scores far lower here than on recall@k, which is expected
and worth stating plainly: finding *one* piece of evidence for a
multi-document question is not the same as finding all of it.

## Retrieval depth

How far down hybrid retrieval you must look before the first gold span appears.

| chunking | median | deepest | unreachable within 150 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| fixed | 3 | 61 | 0 |
| structure_aware | 3 | 69 | 0 |
| semantic | 3 | **17** | 0 |

---

## What the numbers actually support

**1. The reranker is the dominant effect.** It is worth +12 to +24 points of
recall@10, more than any chunking choice. Adding a cross-encoder to hybrid
retrieval is the single highest-value change in the whole pipeline.

**2. Hybrid beats either retriever alone, in every arm.** Dense search matches
meaning and is weak on bare figures; BM25 matches figures and is helpless on
paraphrase. Asked for FY2025 revenue, dense retrieval ranked the table holding
`281,724` sixth, behind prose reading "Revenue increased $36.6 billion or 15%".
Those prose hits are not wrong — a numeral simply carries almost nothing for an
embedder to match.

**3. Chunking strategy matters less than expected, once reranking is on.**
Before reranking the arms span 72–84%; after, 92–100%. A good reranker
compensates for mediocre chunking.

**4. Semantic chunking's real advantage is tail risk, not typical performance.**
All three arms have a median first-hit rank of 3 — on a normal question they
are indistinguishable. But the worst case differs fourfold: semantic surfaces
every answer within the top 17 candidates where the others need 61 and 69. The
practical consequence is cost, not just accuracy: semantic can be reranked with
a much shallower shortlist for the same quality.

## What the numbers do **not** support

**The ladder is not monotonic at every k.** At k=10 it reads 72% → 80% → 84% →
100%, which is the clean progression the project was designed around. At k=5,
structure-aware (72%) beats semantic (64%). Reporting only the k that flatters
the story would be dishonest.

**With 25 questions, one question is 4 percentage points.** The 96% vs 100% gap
between fixed and semantic after reranking is a single question. It is not a
real difference and should not be described as one.

**Reranking did not fix the two hardest questions.** `83,383` (FY2022 operating
income) moved from rank 23 to 16 and still missed the top 10; `72,361` sits at
rank 71 in hybrid retrieval, outside the 40-candidate shortlist entirely. The
aggregate gains came from other questions.

**A deeper shortlist made results worse.** Raising rerank candidates from 40 to
60/80/100 dropped structure-aware recall@10 from 92% to 88%. More candidates
feed the cross-encoder distractors faster than answers, so 40 stays — chosen by
measurement, not by intuition.

## Known limitation

Semantic chunking truncates 2.7% of its chunks at bge's 512-token limit, versus
0.3–0.8% for the other arms. Small, but it is a real asymmetry rather than a
hidden one, and it slightly understates semantic's numbers rather than
inflating them.
